answer: Cedar Beacon Binding: each identity must embed a live sensor fingerprint—a real-time noise signature from its local hardware (thermal drift, clock jitter, RF ambient nebula)—that a single operator cannot manufacture twice, because one physical device emits one uncorrelatable signature at a time. Registries verify signatures ripple across independent observation nodes; duplicates collapse. Attack cost: one distinct physical device per identity plus continuous sensor hosting, making mass sybils physically rather than economically bounded.
